thread:
maya: Heads-up: canary for /v1/generate jumped from 10% -> ~40% after last deploy, seen in rollout dashboard and a few error reports.

sam: noted. any user-facing errors or just routing skew?

maya: some 502s and a handful of users reported inconsistent results. Telemetry shows same user_id hashed to different buckets across requests.

jules: deploy-bot: canary created at 2026-03-15T22:03:12Z, model=redwood-3b-canary, traffic=10%, strategy=hash:user_id
deploy-bot: rollout id=rl-20260315-22, created by jules

anil: what hashing key did the edge use? our LB can do cookie-based affinity, internal router usually uses user_id. did something change in the UI?

maya: checked console: rollout config shows strategy=hash:user_id but effective router config has sticky=true and key=cookie:rw_session. UI override?

sam: logs snippet from last hour: 
```
[router] eval key="cookie:rw_session" hash=0x2a1b -> route=canary
[router] eval key="user:10023"    hash=0x9bf4 -> route=stable
```

jules: that explains it. LB/edge sets a session cookie for affinity; internal rollout hashing uses user_id by config. Two different keys -> different buckets. If cookie wins at the edge, some clients are pinned to whatever cookie says, even if rollout targeted them differently.

anil: current precedence: cookie > rollout-hash. That made sense historically (stickiness), but for controlled rollouts we should prioritize rollout key. Also cookies can be stale/signed by previous deploys.

maya: telemetry: ~30% of canary hits carried rw_session from before the rollout started. So clients pinned to older bucket got bumped into canary unexpectedly when our deployment changed mapping.

sam: quick options: 
1) Make rollout decision use canonical key (user_id) and ignore cookie when a rollout is active.
2) On mismatch, set Set-Cookie to align client to the new bucket (so next request sticks consistently).
3) Add a guard that invalidates old cookies when rollout flag is set for route.

jules: prefer (1) + (2). For A/B tests where cookie is the experiment key we need opt-in, but default for rollouts should be canonical.

anil: also want better observability: tag requests where cookie disagrees with rollout bucket and emit metric rollout.cookie_mismatch=true so we can measure impact and rollback safely.

maya: I'll prototype a router patch: if rollout.lock_key == "user_id" then ignore cookie for routing decision and emit rollout.cookie_override=true; also emit rollout.effective_key=user_id|cookie.

sam: test plan?

maya: local sim: 100k synthetic users with a mix of cookie churn and persistent sessions. Validate distribution target 10% ±0.5%. Also run integration test with LB to ensure Set-Cookie header behavior works (no regressions).

jules: console UX: let's surface the effective key used for rollout decisions (shows whether cookie took precedence). That would help non-devs understand rollouts.

deploy-bot: canary update queued by maya. CI: unit + integration + canary-sim checks triggered.

anil: timetable?

maya: PR incoming today, aim to roll tomorrow morning after CI and a short canary sim. I'll add a dashboard panel for rollout.cookie_mismatch and a one-time alert if mismatch rate > 5%.

sam: :thumbsup: please add runbook note about cookie invalidation and consequences for A/B experiments.

maya: agree. adding runbook entry and linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/981

jules: also capture a few trace ids so we can follow one user's path LB->router->model in tracing. Add trace example to PR.

infra-bot: alert muted for thread 1768123456 (silenced while investigation ongoing)

maya: thanks all. I'll update here when PR is merged and when we start the canary.

sam: thanks — good catch, this would've stayed subtle otherwise. :eyes:
